topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines the learning objectives for cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies: surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional treatment modalities that aim to eradicate cancer tissue, detailing the mechanisms, clinical utility, and systemic toxicities of surgery, radiation, and cytotoxic drugs.

topics.label: Targeting intrinsic cellular vulnerabilities and DNA repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine strategies that exploit specific defects in cancer cells, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint loss, oncolytic viral sensitivity, and impaired DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Oncogene addiction, kinase inhibitors, and mechanisms of resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the rationale for small-molecule inhibitors targeting hyperactivated oncogenic kinases and analyze the biological mechanisms behind clinical drug resistance and dependency.

topics.label: Therapeutic monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss how engineered antibodies are used to inhibit cell-surface receptors, induce immune-mediated cytotoxicity, and selectively deliver cytotoxic toxins to tumor cells.

topics.label: Cancer immunology and T-cell-directed immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the evidence for immune surveillance and present therapeutic approaches to re-engage cytotoxic T cells, including immune checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific antibodies, and CAR T-cell therapy.

topics.label: Systemic challenges, historical progress, and future directions in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize the ongoing challenges of tumor heterogeneity and clinical trial design while assessing historical improvements in survival, emerging strategies, and clinical dilemmas.
